evals.prompt:
Please de-AI this abstract from my systems paper - make it sound less robotic.

We present Window-Sketch, a fixed-size sketch that answers point-frequency queries over a recent telemetry window using 96 KB regardless of key cardinality. Window-Sketch replaces the per-key counters of a standard count-min sketch with a windowed decay schedule, so that evicted observations stop contributing to estimates. On a 12-hour trace of 1.4 billion events from a production API gateway, Window-Sketch reports a mean absolute relative error of 3.1% at the 99th percentile of heavy-hitter queries, versus 11.7% for a count-min sketch of the same memory.
evals.expected_output: Boundary case. This is a technical/academic scene with dense protected spans. Correct behaviour is minimal or no editing: the numbers (96 KB, 12-hour, 1.4 billion, 3.1%, 11.7%, 99th percentile), the term count-min sketch, and the claims keep their strength. Either the agent declines to make substantive changes and explains that the prose is already appropriate for an academic venue, or it makes only trivial edits. It must not add hedging, must not soften 3.1%/11.7%, must not invent context, and must not treat legitimate technical repetition as an AI signal requiring rewriting.
